items.label: Industry: Memory & Storage Semiconductors (DRAM / NAND / HBM)
items.detail: Grounded in the account's active-conviction single-name holdings: Micron (MU, $9.6k), SanDisk (SNDK, $8.0k) and NVDA ($5.4k) form a clear memory/AI-compute cluster; IBKR maps MU to the 'Memory Chips' theme with SNDK, SK Hynix, Samsung and Kioxia as top peers.

items.label: MU (Micron)
items.detail: Only US-listed near-pure memory maker with all three legs (DRAM/NAND/HBM); overtook Samsung to #2 in HBM (~21% share), HBM capacity sold through 2027, ~$25B+ capex funding HBM4 for NVIDIA Rubin.
items.suggested_size: Core holding already at ~1.9% NAV; earnings-cyclical, so add only on pullbacks toward the 50-day SMA (~$965), keep single-name <3% NAV
items.diversification_note: Already held; adding concentrates the existing MU+SNDK+NVDA memory/AI cluster (~4.6% of NAV in Technology) into a single macro cycle.

items.label: 000660.KS (SK Hynix)
items.detail: HBM leader at ~62% share and projected ~70% of NVIDIA HBM4 Rubin allocation; completed HBM4 development (40% better power efficiency, 10 Gbps). The purest way to own the HBM supercycle, but Korea-listed (ADR/local access).
items.suggested_size: New starter 1-2% NAV via local line or ADR if accessible; sizes the HBM leader without doubling US-memory exposure
items.diversification_note: Adds a non-US memory leader; only lightly correlated to the US names on FX/listing but shares the same demand cycle.

items.label: SNDK (SanDisk)
items.detail: Pure-play NAND leveraged to AI enterprise-SSD demand; Kioxia alliance lifting joint capex ~41% YoY ($4.5B consortium) into the gap left as Samsung/SK Hynix divert wafers to HBM. Carries consolidation optionality (WD-Kioxia talks restarted July 2026).
items.suggested_size: Held with +$1.56k unrealized gain; trim-and-hold rather than add at $1,593 (32% off 52-wk high, below 50-day SMA)
items.diversification_note: Already held; NAND cycle is distinct from DRAM/HBM but still an AI-memory beta.

items.label: Kioxia (consolidation target)
items.detail: Pure-play NAND; Western Digital/SanDisk merger talks restarted July 2026 make it the industry's clearest consolidation catalyst, though antitrust and peak-cycle valuation gaps keep deal odds low.
items.suggested_size: Event-driven watch only, not a position; monitor for confirmed deal terms
items.diversification_note: Speculative event exposure, uncorrelated to the rest of the book if entered on deal news.

items.label: CXL / memory pooling & disaggregation (underserved niche)
items.detail: Emerging underserved niche: AI data centers face DRAM scarcity, driving CXL memory-pooling and DDR4 reuse (e.g. Meta's Vistara ASIC bridging legacy DDR4 to DDR5-only EPYC servers). No clean US-listed pure-play yet; a durable multi-year adoption gap rather than an immediate trade.
items.suggested_size: No position; thesis watch. Best expressed today via incumbents (MU) until a pure-play emerges
items.diversification_note: Thematic lead only; keeps the book alert to the second-order winner of the shortage.
